name: Chez Damier
hook: A Chicago dancer at the Warehouse who moved to Detroit, co-ran the club where the two scenes' DJs shared a booth, and worked Kevin Saunderson's A&R desk before starting his own label.
blurb: Chez Damier grew up dancing at Frankie Knuckles' Warehouse in Chicago, then moved to Detroit in the 1980s. In 1988 he co-owned the Music Institute, a club that lasted about eighteen months, where Detroit techno and Chicago house DJs, including Derrick May and Kevin Saunderson, played the same room. That makes him one of the clearest bridges between Chicago house and Detroit techno on this map. He also worked in A&R, finding and developing artists, for Saunderson's label KMS, and released his own record 'Can You Feel It' there in 1992, before co-founding Prescription Records with Ron Trent in 1993, a label that helped define 1990s deep house.
